3.1 Nominal length (I) - The nominal length of a roof bar is the distance between the centre of the hole at the eye end ( or the centre of the pin at the male end in case of roof bars with shackles ) and the centre of the corresponding matching hole at the fork end ( or female end ). The nominal length of an uncoupled bar ( Fig.-2 ) is the length between its end points.

10.9 Cantilever Test - The roof bar tested in accordance with 3.7 of IS : 12464-1988 with an end load T as specified in Table 9 gradually applied, shall sustain this load before deflecting 50 mn measured at the end of the bar. The distance between the point of load application and the nearest edge of the prop head for the uncoupled bar shall be 1 500 mm.

Standard Testing

This Indian Standard as a revision of IS : 8473-1977 `Specification for link bars used in mines' is based on the experience gained by the industry, testing and research organizations. Tests and test~requirements for link bars and uncoupled bars have been specified and these bars have been termed as roof bars in this Indian Standard. Methods of tests for roof bars have been covered in IS : 12464-l 988 `Methods roof bars used in mines' which shall be a necessary adjunct to this Indian Standard. of tests for
